title: The NSCA baseball book: what we used, and what we could verify.
summary: Cross-reference to Strength Training for Baseball, edited by A. Eugene Coleman and David J. Szymanski (NSCA/Human Kinetics, 2022).
access: Verified: the publisher’s contents and four public excerpts. The complete book was not accessible. Chapter presence guides coverage; it is not evidence that we have read or incorporated those chapters.

alignments.use: Programming starts with the player’s role, exposures and constraints. The exercise asks you to distinguish a positional description from an individual assessment.
The testing course includes protocol comparability: measured versus estimated outcomes, different implements and the population behind reference values.
alignments.limit: A testing protocol is not a readiness diagnosis.

alignments.use: A critical-reading task asks what must be standardized and validated before an exercise is used as a performance test.
alignments.limit: Movement instruction supplies neither local reliability nor sport transfer.

alignments.access: Contents reviewed; only postseason examples accessible
alignments.use: The annual portfolio must justify transitions across all four phases, including restoration after competition. This is a curriculum alignment, not a reconstruction of the book’s plans.
alignments.limit: Detailed professional prescriptions come from the sources actually read and the synthetic case, not unread book chapters.

alignments.topic: Total-body, lower-body, upper-body and trunk methods
alignments.use: These remain part of the strength and exercise-methods expansion. Existing foundation chapters provide a starting point.
alignments.limit: No claim of full exercise-catalog coverage in this release.

m06-u1.title: A position is a starting hypothesis.
m06-u1.context: The publisher’s position excerpt provides role context. Build the actual plan from the individual’s tasks and observed demands.
m06-u1.assignment: Compare a starter and an outfielder. List three exposure questions you still need answered before selecting the training dose.
m06-u1.response: Separate the role description from the athlete profile. Specify the observation or staff input that could change each assumption; do not infer tissue capacity from position alone.

m07-u2.title: The protocol is part of the score.
m07-u2.context: The public bench excerpt includes maximal or estimated assessment and implement alternatives. Those outcomes require explicit protocol labels.
m07-u2.assignment: Audit a file mixing measured barbell 1RM, estimated barbell 1RM and neutral-grip dumbbell results. Which rows can you directly compare?
m07-u2.response: Do not pool unlike measures as one trend. Preserve method and implement, inspect estimation and trial rules, and seek comparable repeat testing. A reference sample cannot establish local readiness.
m07-u2.locator: Purpose, procedures and coaching guidance; reference table images not used.

m07-u1.title: A movement demonstration is not a validation study.
m07-u1.context: The public medicine-ball page teaches an exercise. Treating it as a test creates additional measurement questions.
m07-u1.assignment: Design the evidence checklist required before using a medicine-ball task as a testing outcome.
m07-u1.response: Define the construct, implement, release constraints, outcome and repeat-trial procedure. Establish relevant validity and local error before interpreting a change. Do not call a movement score “baseball power” without evidence.
m07-u1.locator: Starting position, movement and coaching guidance.

m06-u3.title: Close the annual cycle.
m06-u3.context: The accessible sample page concerns school and college postseason examples. The contents also identify the other seasonal phases.
m06-u3.assignment: Add a postseason-to-offseason transition to your portfolio. Name what you would restore, assess and renegotiate before increasing training.
m06-u3.response: Explain the athlete’s recent season and future constraints. Do not transplant the published school or college prescription into a professional case.
m06-u3.locator: Postseason examples, Tables 12.1–12.2; quantities not reproduced.
